section: 1. Shared Standards for All Programs / 1.1 Prospective Participant Sources and Initial Contact
title: In person
text: Contact Channel: In person; Receptionist Actions: Welcome participants, have them sign in, identify the program or service they are seeking, and connect them with the appropriate Case Manager. If the Case Manager is unavailable, assist the participant in completing the Request for Services Form, invite them to attend Open Registration, and/or refer them to designated backup staff. Finally, ensure the participant completes the check-out survey before leaving.

section: 1. Shared Standards for All Programs / 1.1 Prospective Participant Sources and Initial Contact
title: Telephone
text: Contact Channel: Telephone; Receptionist Actions: Assist the individual in completing the Request for Services Form, invite them to attend Open Registration, and/or refer them to designated backup staff as appropriate. If the staff member answering the call is unable to complete these steps, transfer the call to the assigned staff member or designated backup. If no staff member is available, take the caller's name, phone number, and program of interest, and forward the message to the assigned staff member.

section: 1. Shared Standards for All Programs / 1.1 Prospective Participant Sources and Initial Contact
title: Email
text: Contact Channel: Email; Receptionist Actions: Confirm the individual's contact information and program of interest. Provide the program requirements, enrollment information, and clear next steps. Send the link to the Request for Services Form to the potential participant and CC the assigned staff member or the designated backup staff member on the email.

title: Step 2 — Conduct Pre-Screening
text: Verify age 18+, Berks County residency, class availability, schedule/attendance commitment, language proficiency, accommodations, basic documents, barriers, support needs, and program-specific requirements. For potential participants whose first language is not English, an English proficiency test will be administered. Admission decisions will be based on the required test results. If the applicant does not achieve the minimum required score, they will be referred to an English as a Second Language (ESL) program before being considered for admission. Add the Language Assessment Score (API/Cengage) in Apricot → Student Profile → View Folder → [INTAKE] Workforce Training Required Documentation. Upload the completed answer sheet and ensure the document is properly named before saving it.

title: Step 4 — Create/Verify Profile and Complete Universal Intake & Scholarship Application
text: The Universal Intake/Application can be completed in two ways: (1) by a staff member on behalf of the participant, or (2) by sending the form to the participant so they can complete it independently. Universal Intake/Application Completed by Staff: Staff may complete the Universal Intake/Application with or on behalf of the participant by navigating in Apricot to Student Profile → View Folder → [INTAKE – Client] Universal Intake/Application. Staff must ensure all required fields are completed accurately and upload the participant's photo ID in the Upload Document section. Complete all sections of the Universal Intake/Application. This includes the Authorized Release of Information section. When a participant's signature is required, ensure that the participant completes and signs the applicable section before the intake is considered complete. Universal Intake/Application Completed by the Participant: the form can be sent to the participant through Apricot Direct Message so they can complete it independently. [Refer to Section 1.4.]

text: Scholarship Form (Required): The Scholarship Form is required prior to the interview. The form may be issued to the participant through Apricot Direct Message for independent completion. [Refer to Section 1.4.] for instructions. The participant must complete the form themselves. While the Case Manager may answer questions or provide guidance, they may not complete any portion of the Scholarship Form on the participant's behalf. Once the form has been submitted, staff must review it for accuracy and completeness and initial the Staff Review section in Apricot. To document the review, navigate to Student Profile → View Folder → [Client] Scholarship Form. The form may also be accessed and reviewed through Notifications (bell icon).

title: 2.3 Interview Scheduling Standards — Case Manager
text: Interviews may take place during Open Registration for participants who are available and able to complete the interview on the same day. For participants who are not available, the interview must be scheduled according to the established interview calendar. title: Welcome Orientation No-Show Process
text: If an enrolled student does not attend Welcome Orientation, the Case Manager must immediately verify the student's absence and attempt to contact the student as soon as it is evident that the student is not present. The Case Manager must call the student; if there is no answer, leave a voicemail; send a text message requesting immediate contact; and document all contact attempts. If the student responds and provides a valid reason for the absence, the Case Manager may coordinate a make-up orientation and determine next steps based on program requirements. If the student does not respond by the end of the business day and has not provided a valid, excused reason for the absence, the student's seat may be offered to a qualified backup student. The Case Manager must notify the original student that, due to the no-show and lack of communication, their seat has been filled. The student may be considered for enrollment in the next available cohort, subject to program availability and eligibility requirements.

The Case Manager must send an email to the instructor and copy the Receptionist and Operations Director informing them that the student is not authorized to attend class until all Welcome Orientation requirements have been completed and clearance has been issued. title: Step 6: Assessment and Welcome Orientation
text: For ESL, GED, HiSET, and Computer Classes, participants should be invited to the appropriate assessment and orientation activities approximately 2–3 weeks before the class start date. Program-Specific Guidelines ESL: Participants must complete CASAS testing and Welcome Orientation prior to enrollment. GED: Participants complete pre-testing and Welcome Orientation prior to the start of classes. HiSET: Participants may complete pre-testing during the first week of class. Computer Classes: Participants must complete the required assessment before enrollment is confirmed. Class placement and start dates will be determined based on assessment results. Add GED, HiSET, and Computer pre-test information, including score results, in Apricot → Student Profile → View Folder → [INTAKE] Adult Basic Education Required Documentation.

Record the pre-test score under Test 1 and the post-test score under Test 2. Ensure that all test scores and related information are entered accurately and completely. ESL Program — Before Pre-Testing and Welcome Orientation Confirm which prospective participants will attend the Welcome Orientation, taking into consideration the enrollment capacity approved for the semester by the Executive Director, including both new and returning students. Send the Universal Intake form by email or text message for participants to complete during orientation. Ensure that all confirmed ESL participants have an Apricot profile created before orientation. Coordinate with the ABE Coordinator to prepare all required enrollment materials, including the Confirmation Flyer, sign-in sheets, assessment schedules, and other orientation documents.

Confirm processing fee or waiver procedures when applicable. Review assessment results with the ABE Coordinator and/or Program Supervisor to determine the appropriate class level. Computer Classes

title: Step 6: Assessment and Welcome Orientation
text: Computer skills assessments are administered by the IT Coordinator. Participants will be placed in the appropriate class level based on their assessment results. If a participant does not qualify for the class level being offered during the current semester, they will be placed on a waiting list and contacted when the appropriate course level becomes available. Orientation Scheduling and Communication (Computer Classes, GED Program, and HiSET) Schedule the Welcome Orientation and send email invitations at least one week in advance. Clearly communicate that orientation is mandatory. For participants who intend to complete Workforce Training with Tec Centro Berks, share the Short- and Long-Term Goals Form one day prior to Welcome Orientation using the Direct Message option in Apricot (Administrator → Connect → Participants). Inform participants that the processing fee is collected on Orientation Day. Accepted payment methods are debit card, credit card, or money order. Cash is not accepted. Inform participants that a student ID photo will be taken during orientation.

section: 3. Adult Basic Education (ABE) / 3.2 Training Launch (Month 1) — Case Manager / Student of the Month Recognition
title: Student of the Month Recognition
text: Each month, instructors will nominate a student who demonstrates outstanding attendance and positive engagement in the program. Selection should be based on attendance, punctuality, participation, collaboration, teamwork, and overall commitment, with instructor feedback considered as part of the process. Instructors should submit their nomination no later than the last week of each month to allow sufficient time to prepare the recognition, which will be held during the first week of the following month in the classroom. The ABE Coordinator will provide the certificate to the instructor, who will present it to the selected student during the classroom recognition.

text: Begin post-test and end-of-semester planning in Week 10. Identify students eligible for post-testing (ESL and Computer) using the current approved attendance and instructional-hour rules. On the last day of class, complete the post-test, confirm students who plan to return for the next semester, administer the final survey, distribute certificates, conduct the class celebration, and provide information about next-semester classes, schedules, and enrollment.

text: SNAP 50/50 Case Manager Guide Referral, Special Allowance requests, and participant follow-through Use this guide to screen students, start the referral process, support Special Allowance (SPAL) requests, and close out purchases. section: Program overview
title: Program overview
text: Students who receive SNAP and are enrolled in workforce training may be considered for SNAP 50/50 support if this is their first time taking training with Tec Centro Berks. Receiving SNAP or attending training does not guarantee eligibility. Kidary and Meralis review eligibility in CWDS and submit the eligible referral to the CAO. They notify the case manager of the result, and the case manager tells the student. SPAL preparation begins only if the referral is approved.

section: Rules to explain at the start
title: Rules to explain at the start
text: Eligibility is not guaranteed. Tell the participant that Kidary and Meralis will check CWDS and will let the case manager know the result. The referral and authorization forms must be complete and sent at least 15 days before the participant’s training start date. The participant SNAP 50/50 guide must be given to the participant so they understand the steps, purchase rules, and receipt deadline. The lifetime maximum is $1,000. The lifetime cap does not reset if the participant later receives the same program through another organization. Do not tell the participant to purchase items or assume funds are available before the SPAL is approved.

section: SPAL approval, EBT access, and purchases / After SPAL approval
title: After SPAL approval
text: Once the SPAL is approved, the participant receives the funds on their EBT card. Explain that the participant must withdraw the approved cash benefit and move the funds to the debit card they will use for the purchases. The Sheetz in Exeter is a recommended location because it allows single-bill withdrawals. For other surcharge-free ATM locations, direct the participant to the Pennsylvania DHS EBT page and select “Surcharge-Free ATMs” to open the current location list. section: SPAL approval, EBT access, and purchases / Purchase rules
title: Purchase rules
text: The participant must purchase the items listed and approved in the SPAL. Do not use the funds for different items. The participant must spend the full amount issued. They may not spend less than the amount provided. If the approved items cost more than the SPAL amount, the participant may pay the difference with their own funds. If an approved item becomes unavailable or the cart total changes, pause and contact Kidary or Meralis before substituting items or changing the plan.

If receipts are not submitted within 14 days, the participant will receive an official SNAP invoice and will be legally required to repay the entire funded amount. section: HiSET enrollment requirements
title: HiSET enrollment requirements
text: The official Adult Basic Education page says HiSET applicants must be 18 or older, reside in Berks County, provide valid photo ID, complete enrollment paperwork, and meet with a case worker to review next steps. The page describes instruction in reading, writing, math, science, social studies, and test preparation. It says students who complete the pathway and pass the required exam earn a high school equivalency diploma. Confirm current placement, class schedule, and enrollment checklist with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: Vocational ESL enrollment requirements
title: Vocational ESL enrollment requirements
text: The official Adult Basic Education page says Vocational ESL applicants must be 18 or older, reside in Berks County, provide valid photo ID, complete enrollment paperwork, and meet with a case worker. The program practices speaking, listening, reading, writing, workplace vocabulary, and communication for work and daily life. The page says completers may receive a Tec Centro Berks Certificate of Achievement. Confirm current class level and schedule with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: General Workforce Training requirements and schedule
title: General Workforce Training requirements and schedule
text: The official Workforce Training page describes adult programs for people age 18 or older, beginners or people with limited experience, who are interested in hands-on trades, can attend consistently, are willing to learn safety and job-readiness skills, and can meet common physical expectations. It says a high school diploma or GED/HiSET is needed for employment, while students may work toward high school equivalency during training; English Level 2 is recommended, and ESL is included. It describes training as approximately 24 weeks, Monday through Friday, 9 AM–2 PM, with hands-on labs, written and practical evaluations, Digital Literacy, possible worksite visits, and employment connection support. It says there is no student cost aside from the application fee. These are general website details; confirm the specific program and cohort schedule with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: Plumbing program
title: Plumbing program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes plumbing instruction in tools and materials, pipe systems, basic installation, repair and maintenance, blueprint reading, measurement, and jobsite safety. It lists possible pathways with plumbing contractors, facilities departments, construction companies, maintenance teams, or apprenticeships. Credentials may include NCCER, OSHA, and Tec Centro-specific certifications depending on the track. The page does not publish a plumbing-specific enrollment checklist; confirm current requirements and cohort dates with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: Facilities Maintenance program
title: Facilities Maintenance program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes Facilities Maintenance preparation for entry-level roles in residential, commercial, institutional, and workplace settings. Topics include building maintenance, tool use and safety, preventive maintenance, basic repairs, workplace documentation, and maintenance readiness. Possible pathways include maintenance assistant, technician trainee, building maintenance worker, property maintenance assistant, and operations support. Credentials may include NCCER, OSHA, and Tec Centro-specific certifications depending on the track. Confirm the current requirements and schedule with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: Forklift program
title: Forklift program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes forklift instruction in safety, equipment inspection, material handling, warehouse awareness, safe operation, and load movement. Possible pathways include warehousing, logistics, manufacturing, shipping and receiving, distribution, and material handling. The page says documentation of completion may be Tec Centro or industry aligned depending on the final program structure. It does not publish specific enrollment requirements; confirm with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: CDL program
title: CDL program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes CDL preparation in commercial driving basics, road safety, vehicle awareness and inspections, career readiness, and trip planning. It says specific license requirements, testing steps, and eligibility details are reviewed during enrollment. Ask a case worker for the current CDL permit, physical, language, schedule, funding, and cohort requirements.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: Industrial Control Technician program
title: Industrial Control Technician program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes Industrial Control Technician (Electro Mechanical) training in electrical and mechanical systems, controls, troubleshooting, equipment maintenance, sensors and monitoring, and AI-supported maintenance. It lists possible entry-level industrial maintenance, manufacturing support, production support, automation support, facilities maintenance, and technical trainee pathways. The page says students will work toward SACA, NCCER, and OSHA certifications. It does not publish a program-specific enrollment checklist; confirm current requirements and schedule with a case worker.

source: Tec Centro Berks Official Website (reviewed November 6, 2026)
section: HVAC program
title: HVAC program
text: The official Workforce Training page describes HVAC topics including heating, cooling, ventilation, tools and safety, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, electrical and mechanical components, and workplace readiness. Possible pathways include HVAC contractors, facilities departments, property maintenance teams, commercial buildings, residential service companies, or apprenticeships. Credentials may include NCCER, OSHA, and Tec Centro-specific certifications depending on the program track. Confirm current requirements and cohort schedule with a case worker.

section: Medical Assistant enrollment requirements
title: Medical Assistant enrollment requirements
text: The official Allied Health page says the Medical Assistant enrollment checklist may include: RACC application; valid photo ID; high school diploma or equivalent; medical insurance card; Social Security card; required background clearances; health examination form; TB test results; drug test results; flu shot documentation; and COVID-19 vaccination documentation. It describes the pathway as preparing students for Certified Nurse Aide roles; confirm current training and testing requirements before advising a student.

section: Digital Literacy program content and fit
title: Digital Literacy program content and fit
text: The official Digital Literacy page describes three levels: foundational skills (computer, internet, email, operating system basics); essential software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Google Docs, file management, workplace software); and information literacy, cybersecurity, AI basics, and responsible technology use. It says Northstar Digital Literacy and IBM SkillsBuild resources may be used and completers receive a Tec Centro Berks certificate. section: Culinary Arts enrollment, length, and certification
title: Culinary Arts enrollment, length, and certification
text: The official Culinary Arts and Catering page describes a 16-week, hands-on program. Requirements listed are a Pennsylvania state ID or official ID from the student’s country of origin, interest in food and willingness to learn, and readiness to work in food service after completion. Topics include food preparation and knife skills, local and international cuisine, baking, kitchen safety, menu planning, food presentation, nutrition, and resume/interview preparation. Students who complete the course and pass the required exam receive ServSafe certification. Confirm the current cohort and any additional checklist with a case worker.

section: How to use public program details
title: How to use public program details
text: Public program pages describe offerings and may-list enrollment documents; they do not replace current cohort checklists or staff policy. Use the page linked on each result as the source, and ask the assigned case manager to verify exact eligibility, required documents, fees, schedules, testing, and current openings. When a website statement conflicts with an internal program guide, identify both sources and confirm the current instruction before advising a participant.
